subject: Borealis - solution fit & technical clearance
messages:
From: Sergio Alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwood.ai>
To: Erin Park <erin@borealis.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-11-25T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: Borealis - solution fit & technical clearance

Hi Erin —

Thanks again for the quick sync yesterday. As discussed, Borealis' plan to embed a semantic search + summarization layer on top of the data lake aligns well with Redwood's hosting + dedicated options. To move to a short technical validation we need a few concrete artifacts from your side and we'll share a lightweight reference design from ours.

Ask from Redwood (short):
- Confirm target QPS and P95 latency goals for the user-facing endpoints (search, summarize).
- Provide a sample workload profile (average doc length, tokens per query, concurrency).
- Grant staging access (or provide representative sample payloads) for the validation team.
- Any regulatory constraints for data residency / retention.

Attached is a short reference diagram and suggested test matrix (redwood-reference-arch-v1.pdf). Proposed next milestone: validation kickoff 2027-11-30 — 2-week sandbox test. Can you confirm that timeline?

If that works I'll loop in our solutions lead (Karthik) and PM (Marissa) to lock integration touchpoints.

Best,
Sergio Alvarez
Director, Partnerships | Redwood Inference

Attachment: redwood-reference-arch-v1.pdf (diagram, 2 pages)

From: Erin Park <erin@borealis.ai>
To: Sergio Alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwood.ai>
Cc: DevOps Team <devops@borealis.ai>, Michael Chou <michael.chou@borealis.ai>
Date: 2027-11-25T11:03:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Borealis - solution fit & technical clearance

Sergio —

Appreciate the concise plan. We reviewed your PDF and it looks sensible. High level answers:
- Target: ~200 QPS for search, P95 < 600ms for search, P95 < 1.2s for summarize at 2 tokens/sec generation average.
- Typical query token size: 80-160 tokens. Documents are 2k-10k tokens; we plan nearline chunking at 1k tokens.
- Staging: we can spin up a sandbox VPC and provide IAM/bastion access for Redwood engineers.
- Data residency: US region only; SOC2 compliant handling required.

Attached the integration requirements workbook with APIs/endpoints and an initial list of SSO/OAuth expectations.

We can aim for the 11/30 kickoff but need a short call to align on credentials and test data deliveries. Tuesday 11/30 at 0900 PT works for our infra lead (Michael).

Thanks,
Erin Park
Head of Partnerships | Borealis Analytics

Attachment: borealis-integration-requirements.xlsx (spreadsheet, 3 tabs)

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Sergio Alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-11-26T08:20:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Borealis - solution fit & technical clearance

Looping in procurement/ops notes so we don't miss constraints:
- Procurement: Borealis indicated SOC2 is a gating item; Laura will confirm the evidence pack we need for the sandbox SLA exceptions.
- Commercial: They haven't committed to hosted vs dedicated — we should prepare both a hosted smoke plan and a dedicated baseline (4x A100 equiv) for their 200 QPS profile.
- Schedule: 2-week sandbox is reasonable but we should break it into: kickoff (day 0), smoke tests (days 1-3), load ramp (days 4-7), failure/recovery cases (days 8-10), and regression suite (days 11-14).

Karthik, can you draft the technical test matrix and highlight any tests that require dedicated capacity or special kernel/quantization toggles? I'll reach out to Laura for the SOC2 evidence checklist.

—Marissa
Senior Solutions PM | Redwood Inference

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Erin Park <erin@borealis.ai>, DevOps Team <devops@borealis.ai>, Sergio Alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwood.ai>
Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-11-28T14:07:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Borealis - solution fit & technical clearance (validation matrix + runbook)

Erin / team —

Thanks for the details. I've attached our proposed validation-matrix.csv and a short runbook below. This is intentionally pragmatic — tests we consider mandatory vs optional are flagged.

Summary (high level):
- Baseline: hosted API with autoscaling for initial smoke (cost-effective). If we observe sustained P95 > target under realistic batching, move to Dedicated (recommendation: 2x p4d nodes with contiguous NVLink for KV cache).
- Quantization: we expect a ~2.0x perf improvement with int8 profiles for embeddings and smaller LLMs; however, summarization quality regression check is mandatory (we include eval prompts).
- Kernel / seqlen: our runtime selects kernels for >1k sequence workloads; confirm chunking policy for 4k+ docs.

Mandatory tests in matrix:
1) End-to-end latencies (cold/warm) for search and summarize (90/95/99 percentiles).
2) Throughput ramp to 200 QPS sustained for 10 minutes with realistic token distribution.
3) KV/prefix cache correctness under concurrent sessions.
4) Failover: model fallback to smaller variant without request loss.
5) Quality regression: rouge/qa checks on 100 prompt set.

Operational notes:
- Please provide a sample S3 bucket with representative chunked docs or grant read-only access to a staging sample payload (S3 ARN).
- We'll need SSH + temp IAM role for the Redwood infra engineers during the smoke window.
- If Borealis requires an on-prem/private deployment for the PII pipeline, share vault/KMS details and HSM constraints.

Attachment: validation-matrix.csv (CSV, 1 sheet) — contains test ids, pass criteria, and runbook commands.

I'll join the 11/30 09:00 PT call (Jonas will be there for runtime questions).

Thanks,
Karthik Iyer
Lead Solutions Architect | Redwood Inference

Link to our kickoff notes + living runbook: https://redwood.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/PS/pages/BR-2027-1147-Borealis-Validation

Sergio Alvarez
